create_sample_integrations.description: Indicates if sample integrations should be created along with provisioning.
create_sample_integrations.rationale: Boolean that provisions example/sample integrations on client setup. It is a convenience/onboarding toggle that does not affect access, encryption, or networking, so it is not a security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

location.description: Location in which client needs to be provisioned.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifier of the GCP project the resource belongs to. It is a reference; we do not constrain which project a team deploys into via a generic policy.

run_as_service_account.description: User input run-as service account, if empty, will bring up a new default service account.
run_as_service_account.rationale: Selects the service account the integration runs as. A policy should require an explicit, non-default service account to enforce least privilege; it must not pin a specific account.

cloud_kms_config.description: Cloud KMS config for AuthModule to encrypt/decrypt credentials.

cloud_kms_config.key.description:
A Cloud KMS key is a named object containing one or more key versions, along
with metadata for the key. A key exists on exactly one key ring tied to a
specific location.
cloud_kms_config.key.rationale: Identifier referencing the specific Cloud KMS CryptoKey used for encryption. We require encryption to be enabled but do not pin a specific key, since keys are team/project-specific; enforcing an approved key name would be overreaching.

cloud_kms_config.key_version.description:
Each version of a key contains key material used for encryption or signing.
A key's version is represented by an integer, starting at 1. To decrypt data
or verify a signature, you must use the same key version that was used to
encrypt or sign the data.
cloud_kms_config.key_version.rationale: Identifier of the specific KMS key version used. It is a reference/identifier; we do not pin specific key versions in a generic policy.

cloud_kms_config.kms_location.description: Location name of the key ring, e.g. "us-west1".
cloud_kms_config.kms_location.rationale: Sets the location of the Cloud KMS key. Region/data-residency is a sanctioned policy target: a policy should require the location to fall within an approved region whitelist; the specific allowed set is repurposable per organization.

cloud_kms_config.kms_project_id.description:
The Google Cloud project id of the project where the kms key stored. If empty,
the kms key is stored at the same project as customer's project and ecrypted
with CMEK, otherwise, the kms key is stored in the tenant project and
encrypted with GMEK.
cloud_kms_config.kms_project_id.rationale: Identifier of the project hosting the KMS key. It is a project reference; we do not constrain which project a team's key lives in via a generic policy.

cloud_kms_config.kms_ring.description:
A key ring organizes keys in a specific Google Cloud location and allows you to
manage access control on groups of keys. A key ring's name does not need to be
unique across a Google Cloud project, but must be unique within a given location.
cloud_kms_config.kms_ring.rationale: Identifier naming the Cloud KMS key ring that holds the key. It is a reference/identifier; a generic policy cannot know a team's approved key-ring names, so pinning specific names is overreaching.
